newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker ahead of G7 meeting.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker ahead of G7 meeting.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Friday at C$1.3903 (US$0.7192) from Thursday's close of C$1.3874 (US$0.7207) under pressure from investors squaring up positions ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
* They said flows were light ahead of this weekend's meeting among leaders of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations.
The annual summit of the Group of Seven (G7) -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- will spend time on its founding purpose, to take stock of the world economy.
The United States, Britain and Canada are enjoying strong growth while France, Germany and Italy suffer from sluggish domestic economies and double-digit unemployment.

France and Germany are divided over economic and monetary union (EMU) in Europe, with France's newly elected socialist government reluctant to commit itself to further austerity to meet the economic criteria for a single currency.
Traders said with such weighty issues on the table and the inclusion of Russian President Boris Yeltsin at the summit, traders were reluctant to wade into the market.
"The only thing we can say is that this has been a disappointing week for the Canadian dollar," Farrill said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 82.71 yen from Thursday's 82.20 yen close and firmed to 1.2433 marks from Thursday's 1.2422 marks.
